title: TrafficGamer: Reliable and Flexible Traffic Simulation for Safety-Critical Scenarios with Game-Theoretic Oracles

control_signal.value: Vehicle distance constraint threshold (competitive intensity) and a CVaR risk-sensitivity confidence level alpha controlling how conservative or aggressive agents are.

control_mechanism.value: Pretrained world model is fine-tuned with constrained closed-loop multi-agent RL to a coarse correlated equilibrium; constraints enforced through a Lagrange multiplier, risk via CVaR, with a regularizer toward observed behavior.

base_model.value: Autoregressive decoder-only generative world model with map, temporal, neighbor and self attention, proposer and refiner, Laplace mixture outputs; pre-trained by imitation.

datasets.value: Argoverse 2 (main) and Waymo Open Motion Dataset; GPUDrive simulator for extra fidelity tests.

metrics.value: Fidelity (distribution divergence to real data), exploitability via CCE-gap, diversity score, collision time estimates; crash, off-road and goal-achieved rates in GPUDrive.

controllability_evidence.value: Lower alpha gives faster, more aggressive, shorter-headway driving; higher alpha gives lower speed and larger spacing. Tighter distance constraints raise the Lagrangian penalty. Average diversity 2.0 versus 0.58 for second best.

stated_limitations.value: Solving equilibria over more vehicles raises complexity and resource use, especially map-wide versus local; the critic input grows with agent count.

notes: Controllability is shown qualitatively with figures; no single quantitative control-accuracy number in packet. Diversity text says four of six scenarios but lists three.
